summary: Feed s154_double to IDS is degraded: 50% of traffic is untagged with required VLAN 20 missing, and traffic bursts to 1.66 Gbps exceed the 1 Gbps IDS port (166% capacity, 10 intervals). IDS has incomplete visibility and will drop packets under load.

findings.root_cause: Required VLAN 20 is not seen and 50% of packets are untagged, indicating VLAN tags are being stripped before the IDS. Most likely the source SPAN/mirror is configured as access port or the packet broker is set to strip 802.1Q tags / not preserving trunk tags, so VLAN 20 traffic arrives untagged and cannot be identified.
findings.impact_on_tool: IDS cannot segment or correlate traffic for VLAN 20, misses VLAN-specific policies and lateral movement, and loses ~50% of required visibility. Detection coverage for VLAN 20 is effectively blind.

recommended_fix.why: Enable 802.1Q tag preservation on TAP/SPAN and packet broker ingress/egress, ensure trunk carries VLANs 10 and 20 end-to-end so IDS receives correctly tagged traffic.

findings.root_cause: Burst analysis shows peak 1.66 Gbps in 1ms intervals vs 1 Gbps IDS port capacity (166% of capacity, 10 overloaded intervals). Single 1G tool port is undersized for bursty aggregate feed, causing buffer overrun and drops at the IDS ingress.
findings.impact_on_tool: IDS drops packets during bursts, fails to reassemble flows and needs_full_payload inspection, misses exploits and allows evasion. As IDS needs both directions and full payload, any loss breaks detection.

recommended_fix.why: Distribute traffic across 2+ IDS ports/instances with 5-tuple load balancing to keep per-port utilization below 80% and eliminate burst drops while preserving flow integrity for IDS.
